video_title: Postgame Media Availability with Coach Daigneault, Shai, and Ajay | OKC Thunder | November 25, 2026

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on balancing winning with long-term team development
quotes.excerpt: we're trying to win every game obviously, but we also are trying to make investments in our season
quotes.quote: We're trying to win every game obviously, but we also are trying to make investments in our season, and in the short-term and long-term future of the team given the circumstances. In the past, we've done that. We've planted those seeds and struggled and worked through times like this, and then it yielded future success and positive results. We have to continue to take an optimistic mindset to that, despite the fact that it has been a struggle, it's been challenging, but it's not because of a lack of competitiveness or togetherness.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on the Thunder navigating a tough stretch: We are trying to win every game, but we also are trying to make investments in our season and in the short-term and long-term future of the team.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault discusses the team's approach to balancing immediate competitiveness with long-term development during a challenging stretch of the season.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on Micah's defensive assignment against LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: he's going from an assignment like Siakam that's a bigger wing player to a slippery player
quotes.quote: He's like a five-man defense type player, especially the way they're using him right now. He's guarding some of the best players in the league, and he's going from an assignment like Siakam that's a bigger wing player and slower game to a guy that's hard to, a slippery player on the perimeter. These are good experiences for him. The thing about him is he's always competing. It's easy to continue to bet on him because you know he's going to compete, and as a result, he's going to improve.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on the defensive growth of his young players: It is easy to continue to bet on him because you know he is going to compete, and as a result, he is going to improve.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault praises the defensive versatility and competitiveness of Micah while discussing his assignments against different types of players.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on execution in close-game losses
quotes.excerpt: we need to execute a few more plays in a game that comes down to one or two possessions
quotes.quote: The common theme is it's a 48-minute game and we need to execute a few more plays in a game that comes down to one or two possessions in order to be on the other side of the result. That can happen in the second quarter, it can happen in the first quarter, and it can happen late. We just have to fight for those margins right now, improve on the things that we know the game is going to come down to.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on the Thunder's recent close losses: The common theme is it is a 48-minute game and we need to execute a few more plays in a game that comes down to one or two possessions.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault explains that the team needs to improve execution across the entire 48 minutes to win close games.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on lineup flexibility and bench contributions
quotes.excerpt: him, Caruso, K-Rich, those are guys that they elevate the tone of the game
quotes.quote: We're small in the second unit with K-Rich at the five right now. A lot of that decision-making was about how do we bridge to a smaller lineup with having some bigger wings on the floor. I also like coming off the bench at times with Jared. Him, Caruso, K-Rich, those are guys that they elevate the tone of the game when they go in there on a lot of nights. We wanted to take a look at something different, we thought it was a good opportunity to do that, but we've been very fluid during this time.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on the Thunder's fluid rotation and bench units: We wanted to take a look at something different, we thought it was a good opportunity to do that, but we have been very fluid during this time.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault discusses the rationale behind using a smaller lineup and the impact of bench players like Kenrich Williams, Jared McCain, and Alex Caruso.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on managing Shai's workload and conditioning
quotes.excerpt: he's a beast in terms of his conditioning and his what he does with his body
quotes.quote: Sometimes he has to, in parts of the game. We want to be aggressive. His minutes were up again tonight. Some of that is just when we're that close to the game, we want to try to go get it. He feels good, we check in with him regularly. He's a beast in terms of his conditioning and his what he does with his body, so we are playing the long game with all of our guys, but we're also trying to compete and go get the games.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on managing Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's heavy workload: He is a beast in terms of his conditioning and what he does with his body, so we are playing the long game with all of our guys.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault addresses questions regarding the management of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's minutes and conditioning during competitive games.

quotes.speaker: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on the team's margin for error
quotes.excerpt: obviously our margin of error it's slimmer and slimmer, and that's just the reality
quotes.quote: We just have to do better in all the little things. Obviously our margin of error it's slimmer and slimmer, and that's just the reality. We just have to win those little things and win more of them to get a W.
quotes.social_post: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on the Thunder's current struggles: Our margin of error is slimmer and slimmer, and that is just the reality. We just have to win those little things and win more of them to get a W.

structured.context: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander reflects on the team's slim margin for error and the need to execute small details to secure wins.

quotes.speaker: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on commonalities in late-game losses
quotes.excerpt: the little things matter so much more, whether it's rebounding, whether it's loose balls
quotes.quote: Just the little things. The margin of error is smaller, so those little things matter so much more, whether it's rebounding, whether it's loose balls, whether it's hand discipline and not fouling. They become more important.
quotes.social_post: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on late-game execution: The margin of error is smaller, so those little things matter so much more, whether it is rebounding, loose balls, or hand discipline.

structured.context: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander explains that small mistakes in late-game situations are becoming more costly for the team.

quotes.speaker: Ajay Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Ajay Mitchell on learning from close-game losses
quotes.excerpt: it definitely sucks to lose games like that, but I think as a team we get to learn
quotes.quote: It definitely sucks to lose games like that, but I think as a team we get to learn a lot about ourselves. I mean, we see it comes down to details. I think we give our all every single night, and in those losses we're able to just see what was missing in a couple possessions, areas we can improve, and I think that's great for our team down the line.
quotes.social_post: Ajay Mitchell on the team's mindset following recent losses: It definitely sucks to lose games like that, but I think as a team we get to learn a lot about ourselves.

structured.context: Ajay Mitchell discusses the team's ability to learn from close-game losses and focus on improving specific details.

quotes.social_post: Ajay Mitchell on Bennett's first career start: Bennett since day one has been very impressive, you know just how mature he is. He is going to keep growing, keep getting better.
